A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of multimodal in-context learning. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-transformer and Omniglot experiments, circuit ablations, and evaluations of production multimodal models.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds Mini-ImageNet experiments, backbone comparisons, production-model head knockouts, and fine-tuning dynamics.

M1.justification: The core synthetic-data framework, two-stage training procedure, projector, and optional pretrained encoder remain unchanged. The added LoRA training and production-model interventions are validation experiments rather than revisions to this framework.

E1.justification: Appendix A.3.3 adds Mini-ImageNet natural images as the secondary modality. Appendix A.4 also introduces text-only Open-MI examples for backbone comparison. Synthetic data, Omniglot, and the six existing VL-ICL subtasks are retained.

E2.justification: The head-level comparison changes from Qwen2.5-VL-3B versus 7B in v1 Table 11 to Qwen2.5-VL-3B versus the text-only Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct backbone in v2 Table 11. The four-model benchmark comparison in Table 10 and the positional-encoding comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 changes production-model IndStrength from sequence-wide attention following repeated tokens to last-token attention to answer-token positions. New protocols include head knockouts on 50 held-out queries and LoRA fine-tuning with a 100/16 training/evaluation split and periodic circuit measurements. Mini-ImageNet introduces a frozen encoder/decoder experiment with class-diversity and burstiness sweeps.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands production-model analysis through backbone head-overlap comparisons, separate and combined PH/IH knockouts, and circuit tracking during fine-tuning. These replace v1's head-strength comparison across model sizes. Mini-ImageNet additionally tests whether the distributional asymmetry persists with richer images; existing synthetic ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are averaged over five seeds and heatmap standard deviations are generally below 0.03. Existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting is retained. The additions introduce no explicit new replication, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: New results include approximately 0.58 Mini-ImageNet ICL accuracy at K2=16 and B=4, backbone head rankings, and fine-tuning trajectories. v2 Table 12 reports Qwen accuracy of 0.74, falling to 0.65 with PH knockout, 0.58 with IH knockout, and 0.56 with both. v1's numerical 3B/7B head-strength table is replaced. Table 10 benchmark scores are unchanged; the new 0.74 baseline uses a separate evaluation protocol.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced. However, Appendix A.4 revises the mathematical specification of production-model IndStrength by changing both its query positions and attended-position set.

C1.justification: v1 presents production-model observations as supplementary qualitative consistency. v2 adds an explicit main contribution claiming that production-model circuits are inherited from the language backbone, causally responsible for ICL, and refined during fine-tuning. This substantially broadens the central claims beyond the controlled testbed.

C2.justification: v2 interprets production-model overlap and interventions as evidence of circuit inheritance and selective induction-head refinement, extending v1's cautious correlational interpretation. New Section 8 also acknowledges that synthetic data understates alignment difficulty and that the progress measures do not exhaustively describe larger models' computations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and names released head-ranking files. Its appendices provide Mini-ImageNet encoder specifications, head-identification sample counts, answer-token localization, the head-knockout implementation, and detailed LoRA settings, loss masking, optimizer, splits, and evaluation schedule. These substantially expand the reproduction information.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Hu et al. for LoRA and Russakovsky et al. for ImageNet. The related-work discussion and its comparisons with earlier mechanistic and multimodal ICL research are otherwise substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The production-model subsection becomes a dedicated Section 5, and v2 adds limitations and acknowledgments, rewrites the impact statement, and removes the appendix overview. Abstract, introduction, and local wording edits accompany these changes, while most technical exposition and section ordering remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Mini-ImageNet heatmaps in Figure 15, fine-tuning curves in Figure 18, and knockout Table 12, while redesigning Table 11 for backbone rankings. Earlier Figures 15–16 become Figures 16–17. Existing displays are largely retained with relocation, caption refinements, and front-page formatting changes.

improvement.justification: Beyond v1's correlational production-model check, v2 adds useful natural-image validation and direct head-intervention evidence, alongside substantially better reproduction instructions. The gains are limited by small production-model evaluations and reporting inconsistencies: Appendix A.4 specifies 500 fine-tuning steps, while Figure 18 extends to 1,000. The stronger production-scale claims therefore remain only partially supported.
